Among the finitely-presented groups that act arc-transitively on the (infinite)
3-valent tree with finite vertex-stabilizer are the two groups G3 = h, a, P, Q | h3 ,
a2 , P 2 , Q2 , [P, Q], [h, P ], (hQ)2 , a−1 P aQ and G4 = h, a, p, q, r | h3 , a2 , p2 ,
q 2 , r2 , [p, q], [p, r], p(qr)2 , h−1 phq, h−1 qhpq, (hr)2 , [a, p], a−1 qar , each of which
contains the modular group G1 = h, a | h3 , a2 ∼         = P SL2 (Z) as a subgroup of finite
index. The free product of G3 and G4 with subgroup G1 = ⟨h, a⟩ amalgamated
has a normal subgroup K of index 8 generated by A = h, B = aha, C = p,
D = P pP , E = QpQ, and F = P QpP Q, with dihedral complement ⟨a, P, Q⟩.
The group K has presentation A, B, C, D, E, F | A3 , B 3 , C 2 , D2 , E 2 , F 2 , (AC)3 ,
(AD)3 , (AE)3 , (AF )3 , (BC)3 , (BD)3 , (BE)3 , (BF )3 , (ABA−1 C)2 , (ABA−1 D)2 ,
(A−1 BAE)2 , (A−1 BAF )2 , (BAB −1 C)2 , (B −1 ABD)2 , (BAB −1 E)2 , (B −1 ABF )2 .
Does this group have a non-trivial finite quotient?                                 M. Conder
